item.title: Water bottler renews awards sponsorship
item.description: ARTESIAN water bottling and exporting company FIJI Water has reaffirmed its sponsorship of the Supreme Award for the Prime Ministers International Business (PMIBA) Awards 2026. The company renewed its sponsorship through a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed with Investment Fiji earlier this week, marking the ninth consecutive year of the partnership.
item.content:encoded:
ARTESIAN water bottling and exporting company FIJI Water has reaffirmed its sponsorship of the Supreme Award for the Prime Ministers International Business (PMIBA) Awards 2026.

The company renewed its sponsorship through a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed with Investment Fiji earlier this week, marking the ninth consecutive year of the partnership.

FIJI Water executive vice president Craig Cooper said the company was committed to support initiatives that encouraged innovation and strengthened the country’s economy.

“Through our sponsorship of the Supreme Award, we are pleased to celebrate Fiji businesses that demonstrate outstanding performance, growth and a positive impact on their employees, communities and the wider economy,” Mr Cooper said in a joint statement.

“We are proud to continue our longstanding partnership with Investment Fiji and support the PMIBA for the ninth consecutive year,” he said.

Investment Fiji board chairman Filimone Waqabaca acknowledged FIJI Water’s continued support of the PMIBA since 2017.

He said through its continued support for communities and national development for more than 30 years, the water bottling company played an important role in driving sustainable growth and creating opportunities across Fiji and the South Pacific.

“As one of the country’s leading exporters, FIJI Water’s impact extends beyond employment, investment and international trade,” Mr Waqabaca said.

“This partnership speaks volumes about FIJI Water’s belief in recognising excellence and promoting business success in Fiji.

“We are proud to have them remain by our side as a major sponsor for the ninth consecutive year.”

PMIBA – themed ‘Economic transformation and exclusive growth’ – will be held in November later this year, and businesses of all sizes across a wide range of sectors will compete for awards in 16 categories.

item.title: Solar to boost disaster preparedness for FCOSS
item.description: THE Fiji Council of Social Services (FCOSS) has strengthened its disaster response capability with the installation of a new solar photovoltaic (PV) system at its Suva headquarters, providing a reliable source of electricity during power outages. item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Council of Social Services (FCOSS) has strengthened its disaster response capability with the installation of a new solar photovoltaic (PV) system at its Suva headquarters, providing a reliable source of electricity during power outages.

The installation was completed by members of the Fiji Solar Scholars program, a group of community leaders trained in basic solar PV technology, who also conducted a two-day training session for FCOSS staff members from July 30 to 31 to ensure they could operate and maintain the system.

The renewable energy system is expected to reduce electricity costs while enabling the organisation to continue coordinating disaster response and recovery efforts during emergencies when power supplies are disrupted.

FCOSS executive director Vani Catanasiga said maintaining operations during disasters were critical because many vulnerable communities depended on the organisation to relay information to authorities.

“We wanted to ensure that our capacity for disaster coordination during disaster responses would be fully intact even in times when power supply was not in place,” she said.

“We wanted to ensure that we continue to support communities at risk, communities at the frontlines, and many of them rely on us to convey information to authorities like the Disaster Management Office.”

Ms Catanasiga said the organisation previously lacked the technical expertise and networks needed to establish such a system.

She said the project would also help ease electricity costs while exposing staff members and volunteers to renewable energy solutions.

“Having seen what communities struggle with in terms of energy prices, and the volatility of market prices, it is important to provide this not only to staff of FCOSS, but also to volunteers,” she said.

350.org Pacific and Caribbean program lead Fenton Lutunatabua said the initiative demonstrated how decentralised renewable energy could strengthen community resilience.

“Every Fijian knows what it’s like to live through a cyclone and pray that the power stays on,” he said.

“This is about giving emergency energy to those that help our communities after a disaster, and eventually seeing it replicated out into the vulnerable communities that need it most.”

He said distributed solar energy had the potential to address the high cost of living, energy poverty and disaster response needs while supporting efforts to transition away from fossil fuels.

item.title: EFL seeks $500m

item.content:encoded:
ENERGY Fiji Ltd (EFL) is seeking $US230 million (approx. $F508m) in financing through a proposed World Bank-supported project aimed at accelerating Fiji’s transition to renewable energy, according to newly released World Bank documents.

The documents reveal that the proposed Fiji Energy Transformation Project has an estimated total cost of $US230m and is expected to go before the World Bank’s Board in May 2027.

The project lists Fiji’s Ministry of Finance as the borrower, with the Ministry for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport and Energy Fiji Ltd as the implementing agencies.

According to the World Bank, the project’s objective is “to accelerate renewable energy development and energy transition in Fiji”.

The bank said the project would support EFL to invest in solar power generation, power grid infrastructure and technical assistance, while also advancing reforms to attract greater private sector investment into solar energy.

“The proposed project will support Energy Fiji Ltd (EFL), national utility in Fiji, to invest in solar power, power grid infrastructure, and technical assistance, as well as power sector reform to engage private sector in investing in solar power,” the document states.

The World Bank has classified both the project’s environmental and social risks as “substantial”, citing the ecological sensitivity of proposed project areas in Vanua Levu and Taveuni, where major transmission lines and renewable energy infrastructure are expected to be developed.

The report notes that much of the land required for transmission corridors and solar facilities is likely to be iTaukei customary land, meaning extensive consultation with landowners and compliance with international environmental and social safeguards will be required.

The documents also highlight concerns about potential impacts on biodiversity, including threatened bird species, forests, coral reefs and mangroves, as well as risks associated with battery energy storage systems, hazardous waste and Fiji’s exposure to cyclones and flooding.

On the social side, the World Bank said the project could involve land acquisition, economic displacement, labour influx into remote communities and gender-related risks that would require detailed mitigation measures.

“Social risks are rated substantial, driven by the complexity of customary land tenure on predominantly iTaukei land, the potential for involuntary resettlement and economic displacement of customary land users, labour influx into remote and underserved communities, and supply chain risks,” the review states.

Before the project can proceed, the World Bank said a range of environmental and social assessments, including stakeholder engagement plans, biodiversity studies, resettlement frameworks and Indigenous Peoples planning frameworks, must be completed before appraisal and construction began.

item.title: Court hears argument
item.description: A LAWYER has urged the Supreme Court to uphold the Court of Appeal’s decision to quash his client’s conviction and sentence. Appearing before Chief Justice Salesi Temo, Justice Anthony Gates and Justice William Young yesterday, lawyer Devanesh Sharma argued the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Fiji-Canadian national Joshua Rahman knew about or controlled nearly 40kilograms
item.content:encoded:
A LAWYER has urged the Supreme Court to uphold the Court of Appeal’s decision to quash his client’s conviction and sentence.

Appearing before Chief Justice Salesi Temo, Justice Anthony Gates and Justice William Young yesterday, lawyer Devanesh Sharma argued the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Fiji-Canadian national Joshua Rahman knew about or controlled nearly 40kilograms of cocaine found in his father’s home at Caubati, Nasinu.

Mr Sharma said the drugs were found in a property owned by Mr Rahman’s father, Tallat Rahman, but maintained his client was merely staying there, had no control of the premises where the cocaine was concealed and had no knowledge of its existence.

Mr Rahman’s conviction in 2021 and 23-year prison sentence were quashed by the Appellate Court, which ordered that he face a retrial as soon as possible.

Mr Sharma argued there was no forensic evidence linking Mr Rahman to the cocaine, with no fingerprints, DNA or drug residue found. He also criticised the police investigation as incomplete, saying officers assumed Mr Rahman’s guilt because he was staying at the house and failed to investigate his father’s activities properly.

Mr Sharma further challenged findings that Mr Rahman had unrestricted access to his father’s bedroom, maintaining he respected his father’s privacy and never entered the room where the drugs were discovered.

Advancing the defence’s case, Mr Sharma argued that “the apple does not necessarily fall from the same tree”, submitting that any alleged criminal conduct by the father could not automatically be attributed to the son.

Opposing a retrial, he said Mr Rahman had already spent more than seven years in prison and had suffered significantly, arguing that an acquittal was the appropriate outcome.

For the State, acting Director of Public Prosecutions Nancy Tikoisuva argued the evidence against Rahman was overwhelming and that no substantial miscarriage of justice had occurred.

Ms Tikoisuva said the trial judge properly assessed the circumstantial evidence, including intelligence gathered during the investigation, surveillance material, travel movements involving Rahman and his father, and handwritten notes recovered during the search, which prosecutors said were consistent with a drug operation.

She also relied on evidence from the search, including alerts by a drug-detection dog and the discovery of cocaine concealed in a cavity within the master bedroom.

item.title: 500km cycling event raises $120k for charity
item.description: THE Cure Kids Fiji 500, supported by Mastercard, successfully raised about $120,000 for the Fiji Oxygen Program. The annual 500 kilometre charity event around Viti Levu brought together 20 cyclists from New Zealand, who took part in a gruelling four day cross-island trek covering Nadi, Rakiraki, Suva and Sigatoka from July 31 to August 3.
item.content:encoded:
THE Cure Kids Fiji 500, supported by Mastercard, successfully raised about $120,000 for the Fiji Oxygen Program.

The annual 500 kilometre charity event around Viti Levu brought together 20 cyclists from New Zealand, who took part in a gruelling four day cross-island trek covering Nadi, Rakiraki, Suva and Sigatoka from July 31 to August 3.

Cure Kids Fiji board member and cyclist Reuben Tucker said they were happy to be part of an important cause that contributed to the wellbeing of Fijians.

“We have had a great four days, and the weather has been fantastic,” Mr Tucker said.

“The whole team consisted of 20 riders and seven are first timers and they’ve had a great ride,

“Everyone just loved seeing parts of Fiji, and you would normally get to see as a tourist to this great country.

“These things that keep bringing people back, the smiles on everyone’s faces as we are going around the island in the big towns and small villages, everyone is just so happy to see us and cheering us on.

“And later in the day when you are getting tired, that is the thing that keeps everyone going.”

Mr Tucker said the cyclists also visited local hospitals and health centres.

“It was great to be able to show the team some of the hospitals, health centres where the funding gets used as part of the oxygen program and it is great to be part of such an important cause making a difference here to people in Fiji.

“Good news is that we are still fundraising as we cross the finish line, we are around $F120,000 and still growing.

“So, we will keep going for the next few weeks and raising more funding from what we have done, and we are looking forward to 2027.”

Fiji Oxygen Program is a partnership between Cure Kids Fiji and the Ministry of Health and Medical Services. It replaces heavy, expensive oxygen gas cylinders with portable bedside oxygen concentrators and custom solar-power systems to provide reliable, life-saving respiratory care in remote and local health facilities. The charity fundraising event was sponsored by Mastercard, Accor Group of Hotels, Fiji Water, Modus Living NZ, and Specialized Bicycles.

item.title: MSAF warns mariners after six go missing at sea
item.description: The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) is urging all mariners to stay off the water during active weather warnings after a fibreglass boat carrying six people disappeared between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group. A search and rescue operation is underway after the half-cabin boat failed to arrive at its destination on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) is urging all mariners to stay off the water during active weather warnings after a fibreglass boat carrying six people disappeared between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group.

A search and rescue operation is underway after the half-cabin boat failed to arrive at its destination on Thursday.

MSAF said strong winds and rough to very rough seas are hampering search efforts and may have contributed to the incident.

The authority is reminding small-boat operators to strictly comply with weather warnings, avoid sailing in dangerous conditions, and ensure vessels carry essential safety equipment, including lifejackets, communication devices, distress flares and adequate fuel.

Mariners travelling through the Lau waters have also been asked to keep watch for a white half-cabin fibreglass boat powered by a 40-horsepower outboard engine and report any sightings immediately to the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre on the toll-free number 1539 or the nearest police station.

item.title: Fijians urged to conserve water as El Niño dry conditions intensify
item.description: The Government is urging Fijians to begin conserving water as the country enters what is expected to be a prolonged dry period, with El Niño conditions forecast to bring below-normal rainfall for the remainder of the year. Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ro Filipe Tuisawau said the Fiji Meteorological Service has advised that the driest period is likely to occur be
item.content:encoded:
The Government is urging Fijians to begin conserving water as the country enters what is expected to be a prolonged dry period, with El Niño conditions forecast to bring below-normal rainfall for the remainder of the year.

Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ro Filipe Tuisawau said the Fiji Meteorological Service has advised that the driest period is likely to occur between October and December, making it critical for households, businesses and institutions to use water responsibly.

“As the Minister responsible for the Water Authority of Fiji, I am asking all Fijians to use water carefully and deliberately as we move through the dry season,” he said.

“The Fiji Meteorological Service advises that El Niño conditions are underway and that rainfall is likely to remain below normal through to the end of the year, with the driest period expected between October and December.”

The Minister assured the public that water supply continues across most Water Authority of Fiji (WAF) systems nationwide, but confirmed that dry-weather contingency plans have now been activated across all three operational regions.

He said WAF teams are working daily to maintain water supplies despite declining water levels at many of the country’s 44 major water sources.

“WAF’s dry-weather contingency plans have been activated across all three regions, and teams are working on the ground each day to hold supply steady as dry weather continues,” he said.

Ro Filipe said WAF has introduced a range of emergency measures, including supplementary pumping, temporary pump stations, pressure management, leak repairs, rehabilitation of water intakes and water carting to affected communities.

He warned that some consumers may experience lower water pressure or intermittent supply as the authority manages limited resources.

“Valve operations, pressure management and the rebalancing of flows between systems can result in lower water pressure, or in supply becoming intermittent in some areas at certain times of the day,” he said.

“These are deliberate and necessary steps that allow reservoirs and trunk mains to recover, and they are what enable WAF to keep water available to as many Fijians as possible, and for as long as possible.”

The Minister called on the public to make simple but meaningful changes to reduce water consumption.

He urged people to avoid washing vehicles, driveways and footpaths with running hoses, filling swimming pools or excessive garden watering, particularly during peak demand periods.

Ro Filipe also encouraged households to repair leaking taps and pipes immediately, while hotels, resorts, businesses and industries were asked to implement water conservation measures, including leak detection and water reuse where practical.

“I thank all Fijians in advance for their cooperation,” he said.

“Every litre conserved today helps ensure that water remains available to households, businesses, schools, hospitals and communities throughout this dry period.”

He added that WAF will continue to provide regular updates on water source conditions and any expected changes to water supply as the dry weather continues.

item.title: Health Ministry weighs compensation for six medics
item.description: THE Health Ministry will consider compensation for the six medical workers stranded at sea last week only after they have fully recovered from the ordeal. Health Minister Dr Atonio Lalabalavu shared this yesterday saying the ministry’s immediate focus remained on the well-being of the medical team, with one member already discharged from hospital and travelling back to Lakeba.
item.content:encoded:
THE Health Ministry will consider compensation for the six medical workers stranded at sea last week only after they have fully recovered from the ordeal.

Health Minister Dr Atonio Lalabalavu shared this yesterday saying the ministry’s immediate focus remained on the well-being of the medical team, with one member already discharged from hospital and travelling back to Lakeba.

He said the final patient was returning by boat because she was unable to travel by air.

“She cannot travel by plane, what I’ve been told is she’s claustrophobic,” Dr Lalabalavu said. “So she was stable and now travelling. And I believe they should be receiving her today or Saturday. They’re all doing well.”

Dr Lalabalavu said the recovery process had been gradual after the team spent nearly 36 hours stranded at sea.

“It’s slowly recovering. And I have asked the team at Tamavua Twomey Hospital to ensure that they have proper rest when they need and limited visitation as much as possible.

“The condition when they got in the mainland, being out at sea for nearly 36 hours, they had muscular pains and minor injuries.”

He also clarified that he had not discussed the incident with Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, saying their meeting last week focused on broader issues affecting the health sector.

Meanwhile, Dr Lalabalavu guaranteed the delayed salary payment affecting one of the six medical workers would be addressed in the next pay cycle.

He said he would discuss the matter with the relevant division to ensure the payment was made in full.
